verdict.rationale: DeepSeek's docs say its API uses an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible format. Users can point the OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs, or any compatible software, at it just by changing configuration. It also natively supports the OpenAI Responses API and can act as the backend for tools like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and OpenCode with no code required. Streaming and function calling are documented in OpenAI format, so tool-calling clients work as well. Missing for 10: independent hands-on confirmation that existing OpenAI tooling works as a drop-in replacement, and a dedicated migration guide listing parameter differences.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can point existing OpenAI-compatible tooling at the platform, or follow a documented migration/adapter path from other providers' SDKs

citations.quote: The DeepSeek API uses an API format compatible with OpenAI/Anthropic. By modifying the configuration, you can use the OpenAI/Anthropic SDK or softwares compatible with the OpenAI/Anthropic API to access the DeepSeek API.
The DeepSeek API now natively supports the OpenAI Responses API format
If you use tools like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or OpenCode, you can use DeepSeek as the backend model directly — no code required.
A maintained function-calling guide with runnable OpenAI-format examples (stream or non-stream)
